Posted May 9, 2002

Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com

By Richard Cowan
See

DEAland medical cannabis refugees, Steve Tuck and Ken Hayes, will be allowed to stay in Canada until the Canada government has ruled on their claims for refugee status. As we have seen from the Renee Boje case, that can take quite sometime.
From 2000, See

There will certainly be no ruling until sometime next year, and if that ruling is adverse, it is subject to appeal. Once the final order to depart is entered, they will then have 30 days to leave to the country of their choice, not just DEAland.

Technically, they are subject to what is called a " Conditional Departure Order. " That means that there is an order to depart, subject to the refugee appeal failing. If they do leave, they could still come back to Canada without having to get special permission. This is much better than the alternative, which is called a " Conditional Deportation Order " which would have made them ineligible to return without special permission.

It couldn't have gone much better, but the situation was probably helped by the heavy-handed behavior of the DEA.

Everyone at the hearing, including the Adjudicator and the Immigration Department " prosecutor " who was very friendly, was astonished when the attorney for Tuck and Hayes announced that despite the fact that Hayes has Canadian counsel a DEA agent, accompanied by an RCMP officer, went to the Hayes home yesterday at 8:30 in the morning.

The DEA agent tried to intimidate Hayes into giving up and returning to DEAland. " It will go a lot easier for you, etc. " Of course, Hayes did not fall for that one.

Although it is not technically illegal in Canada for the police to talk to someone without the attorney being present, it is considered very bad form. And taking the agent of a foreign power to intimidate a refugee from that country is not very nice, and is therefore positively unCanadian.

In the meantime, the Kubbys hearing has been postponed to the 17th, but I have no doubt that they will be allowed to stay in Canada.

I am greatly relieved that my friends are safe for now, and it is likely that there will be more refugees coming up from California as the DEA escalates its war on the sick and dying.

People considering such a move should think their way through their plans and remember the problems that Tuck, Hayes and Kubby have had to deal with the last few weeks.

Canada is far better than DEAland, but the Canadians are not too thrilled at having to confront their big neighbor over this issue. Also, there are a lot of DEA-wannabees up here who think that RCMP stands for Royal Canadian Marijuana Police. Today's events will not please the thugs in either country.

So don't just head North expecting it to be easy if you are facing charges in DEAland.
